defects_found.description: A handful of Hebrew quotations that cite verses OUTSIDE the row's own boundary_evidence_refs -- used only for comparative/cross-referential argument, not as the row's own boundary evidence -- carry Unicode combining marks (vowel point / dagesh / shin-dot order) in a different sequence than the byte-level witness file (2Kgs_oshb.txt), even though every quotation that anchors the row's own span matched the witness exactly on a raw, non-normalized substring test. Content is confirmed textually identical once normalized (NFC/NFD both align, and consonant-plus-vowel comparison confirms the same word), so nothing is fabricated or boundary-breaking; the pattern suggests these specific auxiliary quotes were retyped rather than programmatically sliced, unlike the primary in-row citations.

In the earliest rows of this part, several Hebrew clauses are followed by a single-quoted English rendering that reads as a literal, word-order-preserving gloss of the Hebrew rather than the actual WEB wording at the cited verse (e.g., row 002's 'and he sent messengers' vs WEB 1:2's 'So he sent messengers'; row 003's 'and Jehoram reigned in his place' vs WEB 1:17's 'Jehoram began to reign in his place'; row 006's 'young boys' vs WEB's 'youths' at 2:23). Meaning is preserved and no boundary_evidence_ref is affected, but the quotation-mark styling could be mistaken for a verbatim WEB citation. The pattern is confined to rows 001-006; from row 007 onward the rationale text cites Hebrew directly without full-clause English glosses in quotes.

The row describes the recurrence of בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם at 10:32, 15:37, and 20:1 as “byte-identical.” Corpus verification confirms the three occurrences share identical consonants and vowel points but differ in cantillation (trope) marks, which is expected since accents track each verse's own syntactic position rather than the lexeme. The substantive recurrence claim is correct; “byte-identical” overstates precision by one layer of the text (accentuation).

Two boundary_rationale entries quote and rely on comparison verses (2Kgs.20.4 in M8-2Kgs-072; 2Kgs.18.2 in M8-2Kgs-074) that were verified byte-accurate against OSHB but are not listed among the row's own boundary_evidence_refs, unlike most other comparison citations in this batch which are consistently included in the refs list. Non-blocking: the quotations themselves are accurate and the boundary argument is unaffected; only the evidence-ref trail is incomplete for a reader trying to verify solely from boundary_evidence_refs.

The parenthetical gloss "and all the people stood in the covenant" attached to the 23:3 Hebrew citation does not match WEB's actual rendering at that verse ("and all the people agreed to the covenant"); a more literal translation of the Hebrew is presented in the same citation format used elsewhere for verbatim WEB wording. Does not affect the Hebrew evidence driving the boundary.

The gloss "he did to them according to all the deeds he had done at Bethel" substitutes 'deeds' and 'at' for WEB's actual 'acts' and 'in Bethel' at 23:19. Minor synonym/preposition-level drift, not misleading as to content.

The row states that 'the same full-versus-partial distinction row M8-2Kgs-091 already applies to 25:3's day-only date,' but M8-2Kgs-091 (span 2Kgs.24.18-2Kgs.24.20) contains no discussion of 25:3 at all. The day-only-date-stays-internal argument for 25:3 is actually made in M8-2Kgs-092 (span 2Kgs.25.1-2Kgs.25.7), which explicitly treats 25:3 as 'a second internal date.' The underlying textual claim about 25:3 is independently verified correct; only the decision-id attribution is wrong.

These rows quote and rely on Hebrew from adjacent rows' spans as comparative/contrastive evidence (082 cites 23:24; 093 cites 25:15-25:17; 095 cites 25:11-25:12) without adding those verses to their own boundary_evidence_refs arrays. In every instance the quoted Hebrew was verified byte-accurate against OSHB and correctly attributed to the verse named in the prose; the gap is one of reference-list completeness, not of evidentiary accuracy.
